en: Yes, but dancing. I'm more likely to bust a hip than a move.
Oh, sorry to bother you. I'll just be going now.
No, young lady, wait. I will simply adjust my style to match yours.
All martial arts include dance-like techniques for toying with your opponent.
After all, fighting and dancing have much in common. I should be up to the challenge.
You go, Gramps! Oh man, this is gonna be sweet!
This is no laughing matter, Sosuke. You might even learn something if you pay attention.
Are you kidding me!? This is the kinda stuff that gets millions of hits on the internet!
Never mind. Let's just get started.
Let's eat!
Oh, this is good!
The suspense is killing me.
Hey, this is good!
This is amazing! Really tasty!
Hmm... I can't decide.
That is great! It really is!
Well, let's eat!
Oh, wow! This is really good!
Now that's what I call delicious!
What do you recommend here?
Now that's tasty! I'm impressed! It almost moved me to tears!
Okay, I'll leave it up to you. Surprise me!
Oh, wow, good choice!
Well, shall we dig in?
Hey, this is really good!
Mmm... What a great aroma!
Okay, here goes!
(Hm? Is that Tatsuya?)
Welcome to Tatsuya's Three-Minute Kitchen Hack! Today, we're visiting the food stall mecca of Nagasugai, Fukuoka!
This show is all about having celebrity chef Tatsuya help new and struggling eateries across Japan by coming up with new dishes!
In this episode, we're paying a visit to Todagawa-san, owner of an old-school food stall that's on the outs with the young crowd.
Todagawa-san, we heard you were having trouble attracting younger customers.
That's right. We mainly serve simple dishes for which Hakata is famous, such as mizutaki, but the younger crowd ain't interested.
Thought maybe we could come up with a new dish that could attract young people.
So you want to come up with a mizutaki dish that young people could love, too? Sounds like a tough challenge!
Well, Tatsuya-san, let's hear what you came up with!
Okay, wait for it... I'm calling my new dish "Cream Stew Style Mizutaki Zosui"!
You've done it again, Tatsuya-san! Could you tell us a little more about your new creation?
Sure. It's a mizutaki dish prepared like a stew with white sauce and plenty of black pepper.
You can also enjoy it carbonara style with an egg on top. It's sure to be a hit with the younger crowd, especially the ladies.
Sounds like a feast for the eyes and mouth. Gotta hand it to ya, Tatsuya-san, I would've never come up with anythin' like that. How'd ya do it?
When I first came here, I asked a certain person to recommend different eateries. I was quite inspired by all the new places I ate at.
And there you have it! Another hit dish courtesy of Tatsuya-san! Cream Stew Style Mizutaki Zosui is now available anytime at Todagawa-san's food stall!
We hope our viewers will come give it a try! Until next time! Bon appétit!
(They're serving Tatsuya's new dish at that food stall over there. Maybe I'll give it a try when I have some time.)
Tatsuya's new dish "Cream Stew Style Mizutaki Zosui" has been added to Senbo's menu.
Welcome to Tatsuya's Three-Minute Kitchen Hack! Today's show is coming to you from Tsukimino, Sapporo!
And here's who we'll be visiting today!
It's the manager of Café Alps Tsukimino! It seems he's having trouble attracting more customers to his newly opened café.
Please, tell us more about your situation.
Yes, well, Café Alps is a venerable coffee shop that got its start in Kamurocho, Tokyo, but a new CEO was recently appointed.
He's quite the entrepreneur. He wants to expand nationwide, and the Tsukimino location is just the opening salvo. Unfortunately...
I've failed to attract many customers. But if we had a local dish popular with the people of Sapporo, maybe we could stir up some business.
I see... So you want to attract more customers at your Tsukimino location by offering a local dish. Sounds like a tough challenge!
Okay, wait for it... I'm calling my new dish Coconut Milk & Bouillon Soup Curry Pasta!
Sure. It's the perfect fusion of old-school coffee shop pasta and the soup curry the people of Tsukimino know and love.
The sweetness of slow-fried onions and the deep flavor of minced chicken make it really special.
Lots of fresh cream and coconut milk guarantee that it is creamy and mild.
And my special blend of spices gives it some heat and a refreshing fragrance.
Wow, you're a genius, Tatsuya-san! No one else could have come up with something like that!
Well, I might never have if it hadn't been for a certain someone who recommended a number of great Tsukimino eateries to me.
I guess you could say you need good input to get good output. I, for one, like my new creation. I hope you all will like it, too!
And there you have it! Another hit dish courtesy of Tatsuya-san! Coconut Milk & Bouillon Soup Curry Pasta is now available here anytime!
(They got Tatsuya's new dish over at Café Alps Tsukimino. I'll go try it when I have time.)
Tatsuya's new dish "Coconut Milk & Bouillon Soup Curry Pasta" has been added to Café Alps Tsukimino's menu.
(Ah... Isn't that Tatsuya-san?)
Welcome to Tatsuya's Three-Minute Kitchen Hack! Today's show is coming to you from Sotenbori, Osaka.
In this episode, we'll be speaking with the manager of Montblanc Coffee, a new entrant in the hotly contested market for sweets lovers.
Sotenbori is known for stiff competition in sweets. Only the best of the best can make it in this extremely discerning market.
Our other locations are quite popular, so we thought Sotenbori was the next step. We didn't realize how tough it would be here.
If only we had a new breakthrough dish...
Hmmm... And just what sort of dish are you hoping for?
Well, our menu tends to skew too much toward unorthodox fare, so we'd love a suggestion of something more on the classic side.
I see. So you want something more classic to appeal to the customers in a tough market?
Okay, wait for it... I'm calling my new dish Madame Teruka's egg baumkuchen!
Sure. This simple, yet irresistible masterpiece doesn't skimp on the eggs. Their delicious flavor really shines through.
Rich, fresh eggs and the sweet milk from Jersey cows are combined in perfect harmony with natural vanilla beans.
This exquisite cake is then baked up soft and moist with no artificial flavors or colors added.
Wow... I've probably had baumkuchen hundreds of times, but this is on a whole other level. You're a genius, Tatsuya-san!
Well, I might never have come up with this if it weren't for the eateries a certain young lady introduced me to.
I think you can sense the warmth this cake has. That's her adorable, sweet, and helpful nature shining through.
Are we talking about a girlfriend here, Tatsuya-san? You sure have a way with the ladies!
No, no. Don't go getting the wrong idea now!
Well, it looks like we have another hit on our hands today! Madame Teruka's egg baumkuchen is now available anytime right here!
(They're serving Tatsuya's new dish! I think I'll go give it a try when I have some time.)
Tatsuya's new creation "Madame Teruka's egg baumkuchen" has been added to Montblanc Coffee's menu.
(Wait... Is that Tatsuya?)
Welcome to Tatsuya's Three-Minute Kitchen Hack! Today, we're coming to you from Kineicho, Nagoya.
In this episode, we'll be speaking with the manager of Café Alps Kineicho about his new location's difficulties in attracting customers.
He's pretty ambitious and wants to expand across Japan. He started with Tsukimino, and now there's this Kineicho location, too. Unfortunately...
Business hasn't been very good. But if we had a local dish that the people of Kineicho liked, maybe we could win over more customers.
I see... So you want to attract more customers at your Kineicho shop by offering a local dish.
Okay, wait for it... I'm calling my new dish Bolognese Ankake Spaghetti with Hatcho Miso!
Sure. Nagoya is known for its miso and ankake spaghetti, so I thought, why not combine the two for a bit of fusion magic?
I use ground chicken and hatcho miso to create a bolognese-style ankake sauce. I also add burdock to subtly ramp up the flavor factor.
Then there's the flavorful heat of the aged broad bean chili paste I add, along with domestic beef fat to make it even richer.
That sounds amazing. The people of Nagoya are going to eat that up... literally! How did you ever come up with such a masterpiece!?
Well, I might never have if it weren't for the eateries a certain someone introduced me to.
And there you have it! Another hit dish courtesy of Tatsuya-san! Bolognese Ankake Spaghetti with Hatcho Miso is now available anytime right here!
(They have Tatsuya's new dish over at Café Alps Kineicho. Maybe I'll go check it out when I have some money.)
Tatsuya's new dish "Bolognese Ankake Spaghetti with Hatcho Miso" has been added to Café Alps Kineicho's menu.
(Hm...? Isn't that Tatsuya?)
Welcome to Tatsuya's Three-Minute Kitchen Hack! Today, we're coming to you from Kamurocho, Tokyo!
In this episode, we'll be speaking with the manager of Kanrai, a yakiniku restaurant here in Kamurocho.
Our restaurant has been a long-time favorite of local yakiniku fans, but business has been slowing on account of the bad economy.
We'd love a good idea for an original dish that could jump start business. Otherwise, I'm afraid it's going to be a slow, downward spiral.
I see... So you'd like an original dish for your yakiniku restaurant. Sounds like a tough challenge!
Okay, wait for it... I'm calling my new dish Sundubu Jjigae with Sauce Américaine!
Sure. It's my own spin on jigae soup, that old standard dish you'll find at any yakiniku joint.
My version brings together sweet seafood, rich shellfish, and exquisite sauce américaine. It's like an explosion of flavor in your mouth!
Plenty of fresh cream and coconut powder give it a creamy, mild flavor that's hard to resist.
Wow! You took a classic menu item and really made it your own. I love it! But how did you ever come up with such a masterpiece!?
And there you have it! Another hit dish courtesy of Tatsuya-san! Sundubu Jjigae with Sauce Américaine is now available anytime right here!
(Looks like they have a new dish from Tatsuya over at Kanrai. I should go try it sometime.)
Tatsuya's new dish "Sundubu Jjigae with Sauce Américaine" has been added to Kanrai's menu.
(Haven't seen Tendo since he vanished. Wonder how the old guy's doin'.)
(That was some pretty weird stuff that went down, but lookin' back, I gotta admit that it was actually kinda fun.)
(Well, no point worryin' about him. Anyone who can do freaky stuff like that can take care of himself.)
Someone there?
I heard that! Who farted!?
Come on out, old man. No need to hide.
Forgive me, Saejima. You see, I was busy getting some things ready.
Yeah? What kind of things?
Oh, umm... Yes, about that....
Well? Out with it, already.
Very well. I suppose you deserve an explanation.
You know that magic I performed for you? It's nothing more than parlor tricks.
Tricks? You mean like sleight of hand or something?
Just so. You see, I was a magician back in my younger days.
I performed under the name Tendo Oshida, and my, how I used to pack the house!
I've actually heard of you! Had no idea you were famous, old man.
Well, back in the day, anyway.
The crowds adored me before the bubble burst, but once the economy went south, so did my career. I eventually ended up out here.
If you can do magic like that, why hide away in this godforsaken place?
You see, I've always been fond of big, bold magic tricks. And I always wanted a place where I could try them out whenever an idea popped into my head.
You know that shrine? Just between us, the whole place is packed with my high-tech magic gear.
Ah, now everything finally makes sense. But there's still one more thing that's been buggin' me.
All those offerings... What'd you do with 'em?
Ah, yes... Well...
Wait a second. Are you tellin' me it was all for your own personal benefit?
He vanished again. He's got a habit of doin' that when he's put on the spot.
Aw, whatever. Take care, old man.
Yeah, kind of. You were asking for a job at the Hawaiian pub, right?
Oh! Are they going to hire me?
No, not by a longshot. The manager and I were curious as to why a girl so young wants a job so sleazy.
